papers.title: Modulation of bone formation and resorption using a novel zoledronic acid loaded gelatin nanoparticles integrated porous titanium scaffold: an in vitro and in vivo study.
papers.abstract: Osteoporotic bone defects are a major challenge in clinics for bone regeneration. With the condition of osteoporosis, excessive bone absorption and impaired osteogenesis result in unexpectedly long healing procedures for defects. In order to simultaneously enhance bone formation and reduce bone resorption, a polydopamine-coated porous titanium scaffold was designed, to be integrated with anti-catabolic drug zoledronic acid nanoparticles (ZOL loaded gelatin NPs), which was able to achieve a local sustained release of ZOL as expected. The in vitro study demonstrated that extracts of the composite scaffolds would stimulate osteoblast differentiation; they also inhibited osteoclastogenesis at a ZOL loading concentration of 50 μmol l-1. In the subsequent in vivo study, the composite scaffolds were implanted into ovariectomy-induced osteoporotic rabbits suffering from femoral condyles defects. The results indicated that the composite scaffolds without ZOL loaded gelatin NPs only induced callus formation, mainly at the interface margin between the implant and bone, whereas the composite scaffolds with ZOL loaded gelatin NPs were capable of further enhancing osteogenesis and bone growth into the scaffolds. Moreover, the research proved that the promoting effect was optimal at a ZOL loading concentration of 50 μmol l-1. In summary, the present research indicated that a new type of porous titanium scaffold integrated with ZOL loaded gelatin NPs inherited a superior biocompatibility and bone regeneration capability. It would be an optimal alternative for the reconstruction of osteoporosis-related defects compared to a traditional porous titanium implant; in other words, the new type of scaffold offers a new effective and practical procedure option for patients suffering from osteoporotic bone defects.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及多孔钛支架和骨再生，但未涉及应力遮挡、LPBF制造或力学测试，与用户研究方向关联度较低。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not address LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing (static or fatigue), stress shielding, or surface roughness characterization, which are central to the AM biomedical materials direction.

summary_zh.motivation: 针对骨质疏松性骨缺损，同时增强骨形成并减少骨吸收。
summary_zh.method: 构建聚多巴胺涂层多孔钛支架，负载唑来膦酸明胶纳米颗粒以实现局部缓释。
summary_zh.result: 50 μmol/l ZOL负载支架在体内外均能促进成骨并抑制破骨，显著提升新骨长入。
summary_zh.validation: 通过大鼠成骨/破骨细胞实验及兔股骨髁缺损模型验证。

summary_en.motivation: To simultaneously enhance bone formation and reduce bone resorption in osteoporotic bone defects using a drug-loaded scaffold.
summary_en.method: A polydopamine-coated porous titanium scaffold was integrated with zoledronic acid-loaded gelatin nanoparticles for local sustained drug release.
summary_en.result: The composite scaffold with 50 μmol/l ZOL loading promoted osteogenesis and bone ingrowth in an osteoporotic rabbit model.
summary_en.validation: In vitro osteoblast and osteoclast assays and in vivo implantation in ovariectomy-induced osteoporotic rabbit femoral condyle defects.

papers.title: In Vitro and In Vivo Biocompatibility Studies of a Cast and Coated Titanium Alloy.
papers.abstract: The biocompatibility of a cast porous and with a calcium titanate reaction layer functionalized titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-7Nb) was tested by means of cell culture, and a small (rat) and large animal (sheep) model. The uncoated titanium material served as a control. In-vitro tests included the validation of osteoblast-like cells attached to the surface of the material with scanning electron microscopy and immunofluorescence of cytoskeletal actin as well as their osteogenic development, the ability to mineralize, and their vitality. Following the in-vitro tests a small animal (rat) and big animal (sheep) model were accomplished by inserting a cylindrical titanium implant into a drill hole defect in the femoral condyle. After 7, 14, and 30 days (rat) and 6 months (sheep) the condyles were studied regarding histological and histomorphometrical characteristics. Uncoated and coated material showed a good biocompatibility both in cell culture and animal models. While the defect area in the rat is well consolidated after 30 days, the sheep show only little bone inside the implant after 6 months, possibly due to stress shielding. None of the executed methods indicated a statistically significant difference between coated and uncoated material.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文评估了钛合金的生物相容性，但未涉及髋关节植入物的应力遮挡或微动等力学分析。
llm.why_not_core: No finite element analysis, no quantification of stress shielding or micromotion, no contact mechanics, no hip implant geometry or patient-specific modeling.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估含钙钛酸盐反应层的铸造Ti-6Al-7Nb合金的生物相容性。
summary_zh.method: 通过体外成骨细胞培养和鼠、羊股骨髁植入模型进行组织学与组织形态学分析。
summary_zh.result: 涂层与未涂层材料均显示良好生物相容性，但羊植入6个月后骨长入有限，可能与应力遮挡有关。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验和体内动物实验（鼠和羊）验证。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate the biocompatibility of a cast porous Ti-6Al-7Nb alloy with a calcium titanate reaction layer.
summary_en.method: In vitro osteoblast-like cell assays and in vivo implantation in rat and sheep femoral condyle defects were performed, followed by histological and histomorphometric analysis.
summary_en.result: Both coated and uncoated materials showed good biocompatibility; however, sheep exhibited limited bone ingrowth after 6 months, possibly due to stress shielding.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture and in vivo animal models (rat and sheep) were used for validation.
